answer: Each agent identity stakes a bonded container slot in a shared grove, and duplicate registrations collide in the same stack, forcing costly rehandling. Verification sweeps the meadow of pending claims by requiring proof-of-work tied to a physical resource quota, so mass registration bottlenecks crane throughput and burns capital per fake slot. At the nadir of cheap identity, attackers still pay escalating storage and compute rents, though colluding cartels with real resources can absorb that cost up to the quota ceiling.
